scope: References in manuscript order. Original bibliography verification: 2026-10-03; release corrections for the published Platt chapter and fixed Das version: 2026-10-06. Metadata and stated claim checks do not imply every source was newly read in full or establish novelty.

references.title: Probabilities for SV machines
references.formatted: Platt JC. Probabilities for SV machines. In: Smola AJ, Bartlett PL, Schölkopf B, Schuurmans D, editors. Advances in Large-Margin Classifiers. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press; 2000. p. 61–74. doi:10.7551/mitpress/1113.003.0008.
references.supports: Post-hoc sigmoid mapping of classifier scores. This study uses the logit input and its stated bounded fitting objective, rather than every detail of Platt's original fitting procedure.
references.verification: Published chapter title, author, date, pages and DOI checked against the publisher-deposited Crossref record on 2026-10-06. MIT Press book page confirms editors and publication date. This metadata check does not assert a new reading of the full chapter.

references.title: Beyond temperature scaling: Obtaining well-calibrated multi-class probabilities with Dirichlet calibration
references.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
references.formatted: Kull M, Perello-Nieto M, Kängsepp M, Silva Filho T, Song H, Flach P. Beyond temperature scaling: Obtaining well-calibrated multi-class probabilities with Dirichlet calibration. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems. 2019;32. https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2019/hash/8ca01ea920679a0fe3728441494041b9-Abstract.html.
references.supports: Regularization and internal cross-validation in calibration are established ideas. ODIR shrinks off-diagonal terms and intercepts; it is not identical to this study's identity-centered binary penalty.
references.verification: Official NeurIPS proceedings and primary paper section on fitting and ODIR regularisation.

references.title: Geometric calibration and neutral zones for uncertainty-aware multi-class classification
references.formatted: Das S, Dasgupta N, Dutta P. Geometric calibration and neutral zones for uncertainty-aware multi-class classification. arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.20960v1. 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.20960v1.
references.supports: Equation 7 explicitly penalizes squared distance of a calibration matrix from identity and squared intercepts, so identity-centered calibration shrinkage is not a new general idea here.
references.verification: Primary arXiv HTML, section 2.2.2, equation 7 and remarks 3-4. Working paper, not verified peer reviewed. Its constraints and multiclass setup differ; cite only the prior appearance of the regularization idea, not its theoretical guarantees or equivalence under all constraints.

references.verification: Publisher article and authors' university-hosted primary paper.

references.title: Calibrating for Class Weights by Modeling Machine Learning
references.formatted: Caplin A, Martin D, Marx P. Calibrating for class weights by modeling machine learning. arXiv preprint arXiv:2205.04613v2. 2022. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2205.04613.
references.supports: Class weighting changes the ideal probability target; their model-based correction motivates separating weighted-training confidence from unweighted probabilities. The present regularized-head correction remains an idealized baseline.
references.verification: Primary arXiv metadata lists authors, title, v1 on 10 May 2022 and v2 on 31 July 2022. Cite as preprint; no journal publication verified.

references.verification: AMS publisher article and abstract. Use historical journal name, Journal of Applied Meteorology, rather than its current expanded title.
